The Simple Past and Past Continuous Tenses
You often use the Simple Past and the Past Continuous tenses together.

You can use the Past Continuous tense to refer to the context of a story. It talks about the 'background' action, or the longer action. You use it to talk about an action that was in progress in the past.

I was just reading the latest edition of Mystery Magazine.
While they were staying in room 609 ...

You can use the Simple Past tense to refer to a shorter action that happened in the middle of, or interrupted, the longer action.

A mother and daughter died in a fire ...
The owner told people they were there.
Mrs. Jones and her daughter, Alison, were driving down the highway early one morning when the most inexplicable thing happened.
The police were looking at her calmly and smiling.
I was reading up on alien encounters the other day.

Phrasal verbs are two-part verbs consisting of a verb followed by an adverb particle (these look like prepositions, but do not have the same function in phrasal verbs).
In some cases, you cannot separate the verb and the particle. These are called inseparable phrasal verbs.

It is important to remember that the meaning of a phrasal verb is often very different from the two parts taken separately.

For example:
Matt turned up last night (= appeared, not the same as turned + up).

To turn up is an inseparable phrasal verb. You cannot put an object between the verb and the particle. It must remain together.

Another example is to get off.
You can say “get off the bus”, but you cannot say “get the bus off”.

A few verbs can be used with both a particle and a preposition, making them three-part verbs.

For example:
to run away with (to leave; to escape from)
to watch out for (to be careful for)
to back out of (to fail to keep a promise)

Learning phrasal verbs is a lot like learning new vocabulary. You must memorize which phrasal verbs are inseparable and learn their meanings.

Look at the chart for some more inseparable phrasal verbs and their meanings.

images.text: I was reading up on alien encounters the other day. I came across this story from 1968. Mrs. Jones and her daughter, Alison, were driving down the highway early one morning when the most inexplicable thing happened. Mrs. Jones started to slow down because she saw a flashing light up ahead. She thought that it was an odd place for a traffic signal.

Suddenly, a peculiar glow flooded the car with light. Then there was a thump and something was sucking the car upward! Needless to say, they were both feeling terrified as the car moved upward! Alison yelped and rolled up the window as gritty black powder started to seep into the car. Then came a horrible stench. It smelled disgusting. Mrs. Jones stepped down on the gas pedal. She raced to the nearest town, ran into the police station and reported the incident. The police were looking at her calmly and smiling. They thought that she had dreamt the whole thing.

They sat Mrs. Jones and her daughter down and brought them cups of tea. Meanwhile, the police heard from a local truck driver following the same route. He had also seen the bizarre light and complained about the black powder. Finally, the police decided to go out and take a look at the car. When they looked it over, they noticed dents in the roof. Peering in, they saw the black dust and when they opened the doors to get in they smelled the sickening odor. The story spread quickly. Mrs. Jones and her daughter were celebrities for a few days. Even today, this story is cited as proof that aliens visit earth.
